description: We are a team full of creativity, who is looking forward to teach the younger generations about our achievements and mistakes of the humanity.
summary:
A pixel-art adventure made in GameMaker. You play as P.A.R.S, a small android built in 2040 to fly to Mars and bring back the rock samples left by NASA’s Perseverance rover, a trip too dangerous for any human.
It opens with a story intro and a cinematic launch. Then you pilot a rocket through asteroid fields, stopping for battles with lonely old satellites. Instead of only fighting, you can listen to their stories and choose how to respond.
On the Moon you explore by foot, meet ROVER-7, and calm the dust-covered ALIEN PIBO with a bar of space soap. On Mars you wake Sojourner, the first rover ever to land there, and win him over by telling him you’re a friend from NASA. Then you face the King of Mars in a spooky palace, in a Deltarune-style boss fight full of lasers, falling dog bones and red walls.
The game mixes bullet-hell dodging, dialogue choices and real space history with original music, and it’s still a work in progress.
details:
Rocket To The Moon is a story-driven pixel-art adventure inspired by Undertale and Deltarune, in which the player controls P.A.R.S, a small android sent in the year 2040 to bring back Perseverance’s rock samples from Mars, a journey too dangerous for any human. The game combines arcade rocket sections, where players dodge asteroid fields, with turn-based encounters in which they can choose FIGHT or ASK, listening to each enemy’s story and deciding how to respond, while the enemy’s attacks are short bullet-hell patterns dodged inside a box. Between flights, players explore the Moon and Mars on foot, solve small puzzles such as finding soap to calm an alien or power cells to wake an old rover, and talk to the characters they meet.

The project makes space history approachable and fun, since its characters are based on real missions such as Vanguard 1, the oldest satellite still in orbit, the Sojourner rover and its Pathfinder lander, Perseverance’s samples, and the Soviet space dogs. It also rewards empathy, because many battles are won by listening instead of attacking, and it is accessible to anyone through a QR code that opens the game in a web browser, with a downloadable Mac version as well. Our intended impact is to spark curiosity about space exploration, especially among students, by letting players meet the machines that made that history instead of only reading about them, while showing that a game can teach kindness by choosing to understand an enemy rather than destroy it.

We developed the game in GameMaker LTS 2026 using GML (GameMaker Language) on a MacBook Pro, with our own pixel art, the open-source Pixel Operator font, custom music and sound effects, and Claude as an AI assistant for coding, debugging, and placeholder art and music, and we exported it as an HTML5 browser build and a macOS app. Its creativity comes from blending three genres in a single story (arcade flight, top-down exploration, and RPG battles you can talk your way through), from enemies whose attacks match their history, like the King of Mars, who fights in a spooky Soviet palace with Sputnik lasers, falling dog bones and red-star walls while speaking only in barks, and from original dialogue and humor that give machines and aliens a personality. Throughout development, our team considered difficulty balance so the game stays tense but beatable, clear controls and a readable interface, accessibility through browser play with no installation, the balance between historical accuracy and fun, respect for intellectual property by keeping every character and asset original even though the style is inspired by other games, and keeping the scope realistic for the hackathon’s time limit.
